correctness.rationale: At k=1 the zero set is U+V odd. For k>=2 the Fourier sum vanishes at odd U; for even U and odd V its exact squared magnitude is 2q; for both even it is twice the lower-level Gauss sum. Translation by q/2 gives balanced eigenspaces of dimension q/2. Orthogonality forces uniform vertical parity in each horizontal-parity block, and reduces bijectively to two smaller complete spectra. The unique recurrence yields N_k=2^(2^(k+1)-2). Every partial orthogonal family extends by the same induction. An independent exact cyclotomic cancellation checker verified all 21844 coefficient pairs up to k=7 and all 16452 maximal cliques of the orthogonality graphs for k=1,2,3. Computations corroborate rather than replace the all-k proof.

originality.rationale: Compared full statements and material proofs of the two closest exact quadratic-graph results: the complete prime-power spectral-partner theorem explicitly assumes odd primes and cannot imply the dyadic case, and the dyadic fourth-moment theorem concerns extension norms not orthogonal frequency sets. The other inspected primary papers concern Fourier restriction, general spectral-pair construction and nonlinear-phase frames rather than complete dyadic frequency-set classification. Nine actual semantic searches including alternative chirp, Hadamard, character, cyclotomic and power-of-two formulations found no equivalent all-exponent classification; publication priority remains conditional on unidentified historical treatments.

value.rationale: The characteristic-two parabola is the natural dyadic counterpart of the published odd-prime quadratic spectral-partner classification, but its frequency geometry is genuinely different. An exact classification of all bases at every dyadic level, doubly exponential exact count, and extension of every orthogonal partial family provide strong structural information not obtainable merely from the Gauss-sum vanishing test or from Fourier extension bounds. The result concerns a coherent infinite natural family, not arbitrary finite parameter slices.
